newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Strong buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in shares of multinational companies propelled Delhi share prices to a higher close on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index ended 4.56 points higher at 807.49.
"Hectic activity in some multinational stocks, triggered by the proposed amendments in the foreign exchange regulations act, dominated the trade," said Rajeev Gupta of brokers Fairdeal investments.

On Tuesday, an official committee studying the capital convertiblity of the Indian rupee said local firms should be allowed to access global capital markets to raise equity without prior approval of the government or central bank.
The panel, in a report submitted to the Reserve Bank of India, also recommended easier access to external commercial borrowings.
Hindustan Lever rose 36.00 rupees to 1,237.00 on FII buying, brokers said.
Reliance Industries slipped 1.15 rupees to 303.90 on selling by domestic mutual funds, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro gained 4.00 rupees to 222.00.
